answer: Atlas Drift Ledger.** Each agent identity holds a slowly rotating position in a shared state ledger; every new action must cite a prior entry the identity hasn't referenced before, and the ledger re-shuffles that mapping on a fixed schedule. An attacker re-registering a clone must replay the entire rotation history to reach a valid position, costing one full sync per identity, since stale citations are rejected outright. A haven pool of cached positions lets honest agents skip most syncs. The trellis of valid citations is checked at submission,
